g.text: The numbers that name a row and a column
Where a column sits in the xan stream

div.p: Built by layout.parse, one per drawn line, filed under all three numbers. Every render builds them fresh.

tr.td: The enum id: position in the source file, before any filter or sort. Survives everything.
What the user reads in the gutter, drawn by statuscolumn.lua. Counts within the current filter and sort, across pages.
Index into layout.lines, so it counts the border lines and the header.

div.p: Lives in state.columns for the life of the buffer. Hiding sets a flag and leaves it in the list.

tr.td: 0-based position in the source file. The row id the pipeline prepends takes -1.

div.p: layout.columns[column_number] is the column, layout.ranges[column_number] is the byte range of its cell. One number indexes both.
layout.parse cuts the row id cell away, so column 1 of the buffer is the first column the user chose to see.
so the row id lands at 0 and each carried column lands at its place in the carried list. That holds for every stage below.
Built alongside the carried list and handed to whatever writes an expression. One number per column, for the whole run.
The carried list is the columns on display, then any column a sort key or a filter names, so a hidden column the user is still sorting on comes along.
